sentences.text: The name Chimaerasuchus translates to chimera crocodile.
This small reptile measured about 1 meter in length with a skull roughly 135 mm long, featuring a very short jaw.
Four teeth at the tip of its short snout gave the animal a distinctive bucktoothed look.
Its short forelimbs ended in sharp, highly curved claws, supported by humeri about 82 mm long and ulnae about 76 mm long.
The maxillary teeth were unusual, resembling mammalian molars or premolars rather than typical crocodyliform teeth, and were broad and suited for grinding.

Fossil evidence includes three cervical and twelve dorsal vertebrae, one incomplete osteoderm with a sculpted surface, and a narrow, elongated ischium, though the extent of the animal's dermal armour remains unknown.
The genus was first found in the 1960s but was not recognized as a crocodyliform until 1995, when it was initially mistaken for a multituberculate mammal.
Its multicusped and varied teeth suggest it was an herbivore, a trait that evolved multiple times in Mesozoic crocodyliforms.
A ridge on the outside of the mandible may have supported soft cheek tissue to prevent plant matter from escaping while chewing, similar to Notosuchus.
The genus was described by Wu et al. in 1995, with the type species Chimaerasuchus paradoxus belonging to the parent group Ziphosuchia within the class Reptilia.
The species lived from the Aptian to the Albian stages, between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
